title: Make this site yours
lead: Your gut check on the Makeup by Brynlie site. Take it in chunks; your answers save as you type.
intro: You do not need to proofread every word, and you cannot break the SEO. If you ask for a change that affects search, usability or strategy, we'll tell you why it's there and find another way to get you what you want.

As you read, we're mostly asking four things. Does this sound like me? Does it accurately represent my business? Would I be excited for a bride to read it? Is there anything I want to make more personal?
Almost every box is optional. Anything you leave blank is approved as it is. This doesn't have to be the final version forever: we keep refining after launch.

sections.legend: Start here: five minutes as a bride
sections.help: Set a five-minute timer and scan the site the way a bride would. Read what looks interesting, click what you'd click. Then answer these with your business owner's hat back on. Don't spend more than 15 minutes here; a few answers is fine.

questions.label: What are three things you love about the site right now?
questions.help: A sentence, a feeling, something we captured about you, the way something is explained. Anything that made you excited.

questions.label: Did you find anything factually incorrect, outdated, or a promise you wouldn't personally make to a client?
Is anything important about your experience, personality, process or approach missing?
questions.help: Don't feel like you have to invent something. "No, I think we covered it" is a great answer.

questions.label: How much does the site sound like Makeup by Brynlie?
questions.help: 1 is "This doesn't sound like me." 10 is "I could have written this myself."

questions.label: If you chose anything below a 10, what would make it feel more like you?
questions.help: You can tell us what feels off without knowing how you'd rewrite it. That's what we're here for.

questions.label: Did anything sound off? Too polished, formal, generic, salesy or cheesy, or too casual for the experience you provide?
questions.help: Paste the sentence or tell us the page. You don't have to fix it.

questions.label: Imagine your dream bride reads the whole site, then texts her best friend about you. What do you hope she says?

sections.help: The site has 79 photo spots. Add your photos to the shared album below, named or captioned so we can tell which spot they're for. Each line says the shape, the proportions and what we pictured there; if you have a better photo for a spot, use it. Originals from your photographer are best, not screenshots.
prompts: Arch: rounded at the top like a window. Portrait photos work best, and the top gets curved off, so keep faces below the top edge.
Rectangle: a plain frame.
Cutout: a photo of you with the background removed (a PNG with transparency), the way you stand beside the words in your Instagram posts.

sections.help: These are the blanks still on the site. We ask each one once and put the answer everywhere it belongs. Short answers are perfect, and "I'd rather not publish this" is an answer too.

sections.help: Three things changed after your last look, so these deserve a direct yes or no from you.

questions.label: We wrote "Meet the MBB x SSS team" from your Instagram post. Is it accurate, and is there anything you'd change?
Is every name, title and line in the team section right, and is everyone happy to be shown?

sections.pause: If you need more time, this is a good stopping point. Everything above is saved on this device, so you can close the page and come back. Reply to our email to say you've reached it, and we'll get started on all of the above while you finish the rest.

sections.help: The job of this page: quickly answer who you are, what you do, where you work, what makes the experience different, and what to do next.
prompts: If someone had never seen your Instagram, would she understand what you do?
Do the sections we chose feel like the most important things about working with you?
Is anything getting too much attention, or is something important buried?

questions.label: Anything to change on Home?
questions.help: Leaving the box blank means this page is approved as it is.

sections.help: The job of these pages: match a bride's specific need, help her understand what she's paying for, and make the next step feel easy. "How it works" on the Services page is your process, step by step.
prompts: Is each service described accurately, with nothing included that shouldn't be?
Does it explain the experience, and not just a block of time and a makeup application?
Is "How it works" actually how your process works, in the right order?

questions.label: Anything to change on the Services pages?

sections.help: The job of this page: give brides enough transparency to know whether you're within their budget, and help them see they're investing in much more than the hour of makeup. Your numbers go in once you've answered the details section above.
prompts: Does the copy explain why the service is priced this way without sounding defensive?
Are the minimums explained clearly enough?
Would you feel comfortable sending someone straight to this page?

sections.help: The job of this page: make someone who already likes your work like and trust the person behind it. It isn't your whole biography. We chose details that help a bride think, "I want her there on my wedding morning."
prompts: Would someone who knows you recognize you here?
Is the balance between expertise and personality right?
Is anything more personal than you want your website to be?
